migration_id_rule: 14-digit UTC timestamp, underscore, then a lowercase kebab-case slug; an ID is never reused and is never renamed in place.
canonical_path_rule: The canonical_directory is fixed to db/migrations (any other declared value is rejected). A canonical migration exists exactly at db/migrations/<migration_id>.sql as a single direct child; nested directories, dot segments, duplicate slashes, other directories, other extensions, traversal, absolute paths, duplicate paths, or a basename that does not equal the ID are rejected.
ordering_rule: The migrations array is strictly ascending by migration ID; duplicate IDs, duplicate paths, and timestamp reversal are rejected.
checksum_byte_rule: Checksum is SHA-256 over the raw bytes of the SQL file with no newline, whitespace, comment, or BOM normalization; any byte change (LF/CRLF, trailing newline, trailing space, comment, BOM, single byte) fails closed. An applied migration is never edited; a correction is a new forward-fix migration.
activation_rule: No existing scripts are retroactively declared applied. A separately approved adoption baseline must be attested before this manifest changes to ACTIVE.
destructive_ddl_rule: A canonical migration containing destructive DDL must set risk_class=DESTRUCTIVE, declare the full set of statically detected destructive operations from the fixed operation vocabulary (no partial, unknown, duplicate, or spurious declaration), and carry a structured approval reference (issue:/pr:/adr:/change:/approval:; not empty, placeholder, or malformed). Recognized dynamic/procedural ambiguity signals (EXECUTE of a string/format, DO blocks, LANGUAGE plpgsql, format()/concatenation building DDL) fail closed as REVIEW_REQUIRED regardless of declaration or approval. Missing, partial, unknown, spurious, placeholder-approved, or malformed declarations fail closed.
runner_protocol_rule: A future runner must obey a fail-closed protocol: requestedAction must be APPLY_FORWARD; source validation PASS; manifest exactly ACTIVE; an ACQUIRED advisory lock; ledger evidence present as an array that is an exact committed prefix of the manifest (index-by-index order, checksum, and COMMITTED outcome; no duplicate/unknown/reordered/malformed records). The target is derived from the manifest by id (caller cannot override checksum/transaction mode/dependencies/destructive status) and must be the next unapplied migration with all dependencies in the committed prefix. NOOP is allowed only after the whole prefix validates. Ledger append is authorized only when bound to a re-evaluated canonical preflight (READY_TO_EXECUTE, empty blockers, executionAuthorized, matching id/checksum binding; a forged preflight result never authorizes an append), execution SUCCEEDED, transaction COMMITTED, postcondition PASS, and lock ACQUIRED. REQUIRED PARTIAL/UNKNOWN destructive transactions escalate to a snapshot-restore decision. Forbidden actions (down migration, auto-rollback, re-apply committed, ledger delete, ledger rewrite) are never returned and fail closed as requestedAction.
